extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, and researchers considering or implementing interactive public peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing the Copernicus-style Interactive Public Peer Review process: rapid access review, posting manuscripts as preprints in a discussion forum, open interactive discussion with referees and community, and completion of traditional peer-review to a binary final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: In the access review, editors need to assess whether a manuscript is within the scope of the journal, whether it meets basic scientific quality, and whether it contributes something new to the respective field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a swift screening step that determines whether the manuscript is posted as a preprint for public discussion. The access review is not the full peer review but must check scope, basic quality, and novelty/contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate posting as preprint after access review
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts that pass a swift access review by the handling editor are posted as preprints in the journal’s discussion forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints are citable through a DOI; the immediate posting provides rapid dissemination and a lasting, citable record of the research and discussion (ensures publication precedence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive public discussion and publication of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: During the discussion phase referees' reports are posted as comments (anonymous or attributed), short comments can be posted by members of the scientific community (attributed), and the authors' replies are published. All referee and editor reports, the authors' response, as well as the different manuscript versions of the post-discussion review of the revised submission, are published too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process is iterative and developmental: discussion participants are encouraged to stimulate debate. Publishing reports and versions enhances transparency and documents the revision history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of referees
rubrics_metrics.description: At least two referees, nominated by the editor, review the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually every preprint receives at least two comments by the referees, which are requested by the editor. Editors nominate referees to ensure minimum expert scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of interactive comments and attribution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Short comments (SCs) can be posted by any registered member of the scientific community (named). Referee comments (RCs) can only be posted by the referees peer-reviewing the preprint (referees can choose anonymity or to disclose their name). Editor comments (ECs) can only be posted by the handling editor. Author comments (ACs) can only be posted by the contact author on behalf of all co-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All interactive comments are fully citable, paginated, and archived; all comments receive DOIs. This defines who may post each comment type and the expected attribution/anonymity rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author participation and required author response
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to participate actively by posting author comments as a direct reply to referee comments and short comments from the scientific community. After the end of the open discussion, authors need to publish a response to all comments in case they have not done so during the discussion phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active, explicit responses are required to complete the discussion phase and are used by editors/referees to judge revisions. The expectation is an iterative author–referee exchange aimed at enhancing the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-discussion editorial decision and revision timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: In journals with post-discussion editor decision, the editor—based on the authors’ responses—either invites the authors to submit a revised manuscript or directly rejects the manuscript. In journals without post-discussion editor decision, authors need to submit their revised manuscript 4 to 8 weeks after the discussion. Taking the access peer review and interactive public discussion into account, the editor either directly accepts/rejects the revised manuscript or consults referees again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall decision is binary (accept/reject) but may include iterative revisions; editors may consult referees as in traditional peer review; further revisions may be requested until final decision is reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity and confidentiality policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees can choose to stay anonymous or to disclose their name. Reviewer identity is known to the editor or the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity is optional for referees; however identity is at least known to the handling editor/service, balancing transparency with referee choice and editorial oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests checks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process explicitly includes screening/checking for competing interests for participants (editors/referees/authors) as part of quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review coverage specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Review coverage can be the complete paper or specific aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals/reviewers should state whether the interactive review addresses the whole manuscript or only particular elements (methods, data, interpretation), allowing flexible scope of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript hosting, archiving, and persistent identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript hosting is provided; the discussion forum and the journal are permanently archived and citable. Preprints and comments receive DOIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent archiving and DOIs for manuscripts and comments ensure a lasting, citable record of the work and the review discourse, supporting precedence and reproducibility of the scholarly record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency principles (open interaction, participation, reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: The process enhances transparency as referee comments, author comments, and the comments of the scientific community are published online and are openly accessible. The page lists 'Open interaction', 'Open participation', 'Open reports' as transparency features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is a core criterion: publish reports and allow community engagement to maximize effectiveness of scientific quality assurance while preserving final editorial acceptance control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community participation to stimulate debate
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interactive discussion, all interested members of the scientific community (named) can contribute; all participants are encouraged to stimulate further debate rather than simply preserve their position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open community commenting is actively solicited to broaden scrutiny and improve manuscript impact; registration may be required for posting short comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: All comments as formal scholarly outputs (citable, paginated)
rubrics_metrics.description: All interactive comments are fully citable, paginated, and archived; all comments receive DOIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat comments/reports as formal outputs (with DOIs and pagination) so they can be cited, counted, and preserved in the scholarly record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article-level metrics and discussion metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide article level metrics (downloads, views), impact (citations), saves (bookmarks), and discussion information (social media) for preprints as well as final revised papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracking these metrics supports assessment of dissemination and engagement resulting from the interactive public peer review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility by journal opt-in
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals have to select whether they want to apply the Interactive Public Peer Review; if a journal opts for it, all manuscripts submitted to this journal will follow this process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application of the model is a journal-level policy decision; adopting journals apply these processes to all submissions rather than case-by-case.
